captureNote: Derived inventory of the E2B public capability surface, captured from the URLs in sources[]. Only identifiers (operationIds, paths, schema field names, SDK method names, CLI command grammar, page section headings) are recorded; E2B page bodies are not vendored. Each source records the sha256 of the bytes actually fetched, so a re-capture can prove whether the baseline moved. The hashes are statements, not offline-verifiable digests: re-verification requires the re-capture command below.
recaptureCommand: curl -sS -o target/e2b-baseline/openapi-public.yaml https://docs.e2b.dev/openapi-public.yaml && curl -sS -o target/e2b-baseline/llms.txt https://docs.e2b.dev/llms.txt && then re-fetch every sources[].url into target/e2b-baseline/<capturedFile> and compare sha256.

ratchet.note: Every row is backed by at least one captured artifact, so no row may be marked baseline-incomplete. Raising this ceiling requires a recorded reason; the gate fails on a regression.

unjudged.getHealth: Control-plane liveness probe. No matrix row judges it: E2B does not market a health endpoint as a sandbox capability, and this repository's equivalent surface is Service Host readiness (REQ-2026-0009), which is outside the sandbox capability rows.

operationCoverage.note: Every operation in the captured OpenAPI document is either cited by an operationId in some matrix row, or listed in `unjudged` with the reason no row judges it. 70 of 71 are cited; the single exception is the control-plane liveness probe, which is not a sandbox capability. A future row that judges an operation must cite it here, and the corresponding `unjudged` entry must then be deleted: the involution is enforced both ways.

rustWorkspace.note: The Rust side cannot be recomputed from source the way the contract suite can: the number only exists after a build and a run, so this is a measurement recorded next to the command that produced it, in the same sense as the source sha256 values. `cargo test --workspace` was run twice while writing this record and reported 67 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored both times; the ignored test is the one that declares it needs an external PostgreSQL.

testInventory.note: The contract suite's declared size, recomputed from the files. The audit document quotes these numbers in its test-coverage section, so a stale reading there is a documentation falsehood: this record fails the gate when either side moves without the other. `rustWorkspace` is a measurement, not a recomputation, and is compared against the document rather than the source.
